A few people asked why my latest book focuses on Elijah. Shouldn’t we as believers focus on Jesus?
Consider this. When Jesus was transfigured in glory on the mountain, His face shining like the sun, who did the Father send to stand with Him? Moses and Elijah. The Law and the Prophets, standing on either side of the Messiah. In Matthew 17:3, we read that “Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with Him.” That is not a small detail. Of all the giants in Israel’s history, Elijah is chosen to represent every prophet who ever spoke for God.

And the record goes further. When the crowds tried to guess who Jesus was, many of them said, “He is Elijah.” When Jesus spoke of John the Baptist, He said John came in the spirit and power of Elijah. The very last verse of the Old Testament, in Malachi, promised that God will send Elijah before the great and dreadful day of the Lord.

So Elijah stands at both ends of the story. He points forward to John, who prepared the way for the first coming, and he points forward again to the days before the second coming. This man is woven right through the ministry of Jesus from beginning to end. 

Once I saw how deeply connected they were, I could not read his story the same way again. That connection is at the heart of ‘The Elijah Mandate’.

So here’s my answer to the opening question: a deep study of the word of God and of the characters most pivotal to Jesus’ ministry are how we focus on Jesus. 

Pre-order ‘The Elijah Mandate’ today. Once you’ve read the book, you’ll not only know more about Elijah, you will see Jesus more clearly than you ever have. And every pre-order tells the bookstores the same thing God told Elijah on that mountain – there are far more of us around than the world thinks.

Preorder your copy of The Elijah Mandate today: https://linktw.in/The-Elijah-Mandate
